## init · INIT1-design — init and the boot manifest: cut it into packages

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 5

Evidence: Owner approved 2026-09-29; written in 7e29a424c (signed off): boot.md, budgets.md, devices.md, init.md, netd.md, consoled.md, testbench.md, m1-separation.md. Nodes INIT1 (loader loads kernel+init, device_info call, tester in init's place, TAKE_GIFTS gone; needs GATE1+API1), INIT2 (init, manifest, checks, servers, mkimage), INIT3 (restarts, grant release, rollback, netd restart), INIT4 (net cases under init, rig.rs deleted). Owner decisions: the cut and pages; a tester in init's place for kernel cases (R33, no exception); device_info as the 27th call; consoled prefixes non-init lines with [con N].

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `37a8228b8fb3aa6ba9cf726e392c304b` · 2026-09-29T14:42:47Z

> init: the package cut and three design choices
> 
> 1. Sign off the init cut and the page text (uncommitted, docs checker clean: boot.md, budgets.md, devices.md, init.md, netd.md, consoled.md, testbench.md, the M1 page)? Four Tier A packages in a chain. INIT1 (L): the loader loads only the kernel and init, maps the bundle and a device list into init; kernel cases run a tester in init's place. INIT2 (L): init with the manifest, its checks, the endpoints and starting consoled, keyd, bootfsd, blkd, netd, ipd. INIT3 (M): restarts, grant release, rollback in a boot, a netd restart case. INIT4 (M): the net cases boot init and the net rig goes. Decided from the tenets, not asked: the kernel keeps sizing system (root keeps one process for init; the manifest's `system` entry goes); weights unchanged; init owns every server endpoint (in root) so a restart keeps it; a restart uses a fresh budget; a quarantined driver reboots the box; netd restarts like any driver (ipd already retries); blame waits for the steward.
>    - Approve (recommended): Commit the pages; INIT1 launches after GATE1.
>    - Change it: Say what.
> 2. Kernel cases need root and system budgets, and R33 forbids init handing either to any program. Once the loader starts only init, how do they run? (The plan page said 'through init'.)
>    - Tester in init's place (recommended): Recommended. The case's first program is packed as the second entry and gets init's handoff. The log server launches the rest through the stub with the budgets the case names, so TAKE_GIFTS goes. The real init has no bench mode and R33 has no exception. The servers' cases boot the real init with a manifest of their own.
>    - A test build of init: A test-only init feature hands the case its programs and budgets. That puts a test path in the most privileged process, even if compiled out.
>    - An R33 exception: A manifest entry that may grant system budgets to test programs. This weakens R33 for every manifest.
> 3. The kernel hands init device handles without saying which device each is, and the manifest names devices by device-tree node path. How does init match them?
>    - Loader's device list (recommended): Recommended. The loader, which already reads the tree, maps one read-only page into init listing each device handle's kind, DMA flag and node path, in handle order, written from the same record as Devs. No kernel change beyond moving the 16-DMA-device cap into the loader (the kernel then refuses more instead of skipping).
>    - A kernel call: A new call returns a device handle's base address or IRQ number, and the manifest names devices by address. This adds a 27th call and a kernel ABI and model change, and the kernel starts saying which device a handle names.
> 4. Under init, programs write through consoled, which today writes bytes as they come, so any program could print init's verdict lines. The bench's rule F and the system console both need to know who wrote a line.
>    - consoled prefixes (recommended): Recommended. Writes through init's root connection go out bare. Every line from a minted connection starts with `[con N] `, N being its connection id, which init prints bare when it starts each child. If the writer changes mid-line, consoled ends the line first. This is the log server's badge prefix, moved into consoled.
>    - No attribution: consoled stays raw, and cases under init judge only from outside (peers, captures, power-off status). In-guest checks like the net rig's then have no trusted voice.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `fde47a647512c593665c48e87f027868` · 2026-09-29T14:53:44Z

> Answered, owner signed off. Pages committed on redoubt, 7e29a424c: boot.md, budgets.md, devices.md, init.md, netd.md, consoled.md, testbench.md and the M1 page. Staged by path; doccheck clean.
> 1. Nodes (not started, Tier A, in a chain): INIT1 (L, needs GATE1+API1): the loader loads only the kernel and init, and maps the bundle into init (a0/a1). The new call device_info. Root keeps init's process. Kernel cases run a tester in init's place, and TAKE_GIFTS goes. INIT2 (L): init with the manifest, checks, endpoints and starting the servers; consoled attribution; bucket counts; ./mkimage from image/boot.toml. INIT3 (M): restarts, grant release, rollback in a boot, the netd restart case. INIT4 (M): the net cases under init; rig.rs deleted. The init step now also needs INIT4.
> 2. Open items settled on the pages:
> - The bundle is mapped into init, charged to root.
> - Devices: the device tree and the manifest decide together, and the manifest names devices by register base and interrupt. Drivers find handles by name. init keeps copies of device handles but never maps one. A quarantined driver reboots the box.
> - The kernel sizes system; root keeps one process; weights are unchanged.
> - init owns server endpoints in root, and a restart uses a fresh budget.
> - netd restarts like any driver.
> - The data-entry read-back case and ./mkimage's builder are specified.
> Blame waits for the steward.
> 3. .wash/local/INIT1-implementer.md.
> Owner decisions: approve the cut and pages; a tester in init's place for kernel cases (R33 keeps no exception); a kernel call, device_info (the 27th call: ABI, model, case), over a loader-written device list; consoled prefixes every line but init's with `[con N] `.
